# ARCH-16: Use the weakest spatial reference the job needs, and name the one you use

- A position is relative to the EKF origin (NED from the AHRS) and needs no absolute reference: a flow-only copter has one with no GPS and no origin. A location is latitude, longitude and altitude; converting between the two needs the EKF origin (`Location::get_vector_from_origin_NEU()` asks the AHRS for it), and an absolute location needs an absolute source such as GPS. The EKF origin is the frame positions are measured in: once valid its horizontal position never moves, and its altitude is re-referenced only by a height datum reset on the ground ([#32768](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/32768) works towards making the origin fully immutable). Home is where the vehicle returns to, and it can move: a GCS can set it at any time, and Plane moves it while disarmed.
- Ask for the weakest of these that does the job: nothing where no spatial reference is needed, a position where a position will do, a location only where an absolute fix is genuinely required, and home or origin only as what each is. On Copter home is not the origin, most modes need only a position (`requires_position()`), RTL needs home and lat/lon targets need the origin; on Plane home and origin are set together from the first good GPS fixes and kept together while disarmed, and it navigates by locations. Never move the origin's horizontal position, do not change the altitude reference a vehicle measures against from one flight to the next, and use home-relative height for above-home semantics (peterbarker, [#31619](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/31619): "home is not the same as origin"; rmackay9, [#32505](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/32505): the position controller relies on the origin not moving).
